page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc5.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6149 processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes 22 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate mixed performance profiles. The instance demonstrates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7203.49 and a Passmark CPU score of 8280.79. It also shows average capabilities in specific tasks such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and text processing. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1091.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1355.68. Memory performance is also constrained, with uncached large-block read bandwidth scoring in the bottom 25% at 38.98 GB/sec, and database operations and Redis SET operations registering weak performance.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfc5.2xlarge offers a compute-focused hardware profile without the overhead of bundled local storage. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring dedicated, steady-state CPU resources rather than massive memory footprints or high-speed local disk I/O. Appropriate workloads include moderate multi-threaded compute tasks, software compilation, text processing, and lightweight web serving, whereas it is less recommended for memory-intensive databases, large-scale LLM inference, or high-throughput storage operations.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 2.0 GB of memory per core, 22 MB of L3 cache, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, with no local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks reveal average multi-core capabilities, including a Passmark CPU score of 8280.79 and solid software compilation speeds, contrasted with weaker single-core and uncached memory read performance. This resource profile is appropriate for moderate multi-threaded compute workloads, text processing, and software compilation tasks that require dedicated CPU allocation without demanding high memory density or local storage.
